heroHeadline: IFT-12 NET Adjusts to May 20 (T-1 Day at Starbase) — Starship V3 Terminal Countdown; Artemis II Crew Day 38 at JSC
heroSubtitle: May 18: SpaceX Starship IFT-12 (Booster 19 + Ship 39 — Starship V3 debut) entered T-1 day terminal countdown at Orbital Launch Pad 2, Starbase, as the Net Earliest Timing was quietly adjusted one day to May 20, 2026 at 5:30 PM CDT (22:30 UTC) — no anomaly reported, vehicle is healthy and GO. T-1 operations included final avionics checks, propellant timeline coordination, Eastern Range safety polling, and weather confirmation. IFT-12 is the first launch from Starbase's second orbital pad (OLP-2), the maiden flight of 33 Raptor 3 engines, and the first Starship to carry a pressurized docking port and propellant-transfer interface hardware — all NASA-mandated precursors for Artemis III HLS qualification. The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen (CSA) — are at Johnson Space Center on Day 38 post-splashdown (Orion splashed down April 10, 2026 at 8:07 p.m. EDT), continuing post-flight physiological reconditioning and mission debriefs. At KSC's Multi-Payload Processing Facility, Orion heat shield visual inspection continues; formal Marshall X-ray scans and Avcoat sample extractions remain on track for summer 2026. Artemis III SLS core stage stacking advances in VAB High Bay 2. Artemis Accords at 67 nations. House Appropriations full committee markup (May 13) recommends $24.438B for NASA — flat with FY2026, rejecting the White House 23% cut.
